subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Does a hostile browser origin have a supported current-main path to invoke `/api/v1/admin/rpc` and mutate configuration without possessing Gateway credentials or passing the intended trusted-ingress boundary?
rationale: The public report targets stale or incorrect ACP entry points, while the only documented HTTP admin route is optional and has multiple materially different authentication modes; accepting or rejecting the security claim requires a controlled boundary test.

options.title: Request private current-main proof
options.body: Ask for an exact route, auth configuration, request headers/body, browser trace, and successful configuration mutation through the private security channel before changing code.

options.title: Harden mutating HTTP routes
options.body: Adopt centralized browser-origin or anti-CSRF enforcement for authenticated state-changing HTTP routes as defense in depth even if the reported ACP path is incorrect.

options.title: Close as unsubstantiated
options.body: Close after security review if no browser-reachable mutation can be demonstrated against the supported Gateway HTTP surfaces.

recommendation.title: Request private current-main proof
recommendation.body: Ask for an exact route, auth configuration, request headers/body, browser trace, and successful configuration mutation through the private security channel before changing code.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision concerns the Gateway HTTP authentication and browser-origin contract rather than ACP session internals.
